paper.title: How can extremism prevail? A study based on the relative agreement interaction model
paper.journal: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation 5(4):1

headline: Deffuant-Amblard 2002 relative-agreement w/ extremists (agent-based): 1/3 locked clauses REPRO; P1 capture=0.408 (bar<0.15), P2 y=0.506 (double-extreme), P3 single-pole frac=0.00 (bar>=0.60)

verdicts.gate: P1 central convergence (U=0.4, delta=0): y<0.1 AND moderate-capture<0.15 AND central|x|<0.3
P2 double-extreme (U=1.2, delta=0): y in [0.35,0.65] AND moderate-capture>0.6 AND |mean x|<0.2
P3 single-extreme (U=1.4, delta=0.1): >=60% of seeds one pole >0.9 & opposite <0.1, captured pole = + majority in >=80% of those
reasons: single-pole fraction = 0.000 (0/20 seeds with one pole >0.9 and the opposite <0.1); need >= 0.6
among single-pole seeds, + pole won in 0.000 (0/0); need >= 0.8 (vacuously unmet when no seed is single-pole)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce central/double/single-extreme regimes of the relative-agreement model and would catch an artifact

citations: Deffuant, G., Amblard, F., Weisbuch, G., Faure, T. (2002). How can extremism prevail? A study based on the relative agreement interaction model. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation 5(4):1. https://www.jasss.org/5/4/1.html

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the locked polarization metric y = p'_+^2 + p'_-^2 over the initially-moderate agents
